page.layout: One page of text in one column, with running head and page number at the top. Signature at the bottom left.

p.i: ferè ac nominatim parentem suum appellet: neq; iniuria, cum idem Lampridius testetur, eum Imperatorem iccirco summum fuisse, quòd Vlpiani præcipuè consilijs suam Rempub. administrarit.

Adiunxi etiam eodem in libello controversiarum tractandarũ rationem quandam artificiosam, olim ab Hermagora, rhetore & iurisconsulto vetustissimo peracutè sanè et persubtiliter excogitatam: nostris vero temporibus planè vel neglectam, vel ignoratam: quam ego tribus hisce annis, quibus sum in hac schola Ius civile interpretatus, in lucem ex tenebris longo intervallo educere sum conatus: verissimum de ea Ciceronis esse testimonium re ipsa expertus, qui in Bruto disciplinam Hermagoræ ad inveniendũ expeditam esse ait, rationesq; certas dare, quæ ordinem habeant, & quasdam errare in docendo non patientes vias. Ut mihi quidem minimè dubitandum esse videatur,

page.notes: The signature "4 3" at the bottom left is uncertain; the second figure may be a different mark. The "neq;" abbreviation before "iniuria" has a small mark that may be a superscript sign and is read as "neq;" with some doubt. The word "testimonium" is split across lines "te / stimonium" without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The paragraph opening "Adiunxi" is marked by a decorative sign before the first letter.
